problem: Existing scene graphs encode only spatial or only functional relations, are static snapshots without object-state updates, and are not task-conditioned. Direct VLM planning from raw images is also unreliable for multi-step household tasks.
motivation: Mobile manipulators must both navigate and manipulate, so they need a compact representation of where objects are, how they function, and which parts are actionable. Humans attend to task-relevant information dynamically, and this motivates task-oriented graphs with part-level nodes. A motivating experiment shows that GPT-5 planning directly from images misses prerequisite steps.
key_idea: Train a 7B VLM with RL (DAPO with a graph-alignment reward) to generate instruction-conditioned scene graphs that unify spatial and functional edges and include part-level nodes, then plan from that graph (Graph-then-Plan).
insight: A unified spatial+functional graph beats single-relation graphs for both Qwen-based and LLaVA-OV-based models (MomaGraph-R1 overall 59.9 spatial-only, 64.9 functional-only, 71.6 unified). Graph-then-Plan improves nearly every model over direct planning, and RL beats SFT (63.9) and ICL (60.2) with the same data (71.6). Reward-weight sensitivity is low.
method: MomaGraph representation: task-oriented graph G_T=(N, E_s, E_f) built from multi-view images and an instruction, with directed spatial (9 types) and functional (6 types) edges from triggering to affected object, and part-level nodes such as handles, knobs and buttons

Graph-alignment reward: R = w_a(R_action + R_edges + R_nodes) + w_f R_format + w_l R_length. R_edges is a max-matched semantic similarity over spatial and functional labels, R_nodes is the IoU of node sets, and R_action is an exact match on action type
MomaGraph-R1 training: Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct trained with DAPO in EasyR1 (8×A100, ~13h, 175 steps, lr 1e-6, 5 rollouts)
Graph-then-Plan: the same VLM first outputs a JSON task-specific scene graph and then produces the action plan conditioned on it, acting as a zero-shot planner

State-aware dynamic update: after each action and observation, G^(t+1)=U(G^(t), a_t, s_{t+1}) prunes inconsistent one-to-many functional hypotheses (e.g. which knob controls the burner) and keeps confirmed ones
MomaGraph-Scenes dataset: ~1,050 task subgraphs, 6,278 multi-view images, >350 scenes, 93 instructions, from real-world capture, re-annotated OpenFunGraph/SceneFun3D, and AI2-THOR
MomaGraph-Bench: multiple-choice VQA with 294 scenes, 1,446 images and 352 graphs, covering six reasoning capabilities across four tiers (T1 single-step to T4 dynamic replanning)

setting.training_data: MomaGraph-Scenes: ~1,050 task-oriented subgraphs / 6,278 multi-view RGB images (real-world, OpenFunGraph, SceneFun3D, AI2-THOR)
setting.observation: multi-view RGB images + natural language instruction (RGB-D on the real robot)
setting.action_space: high-level symbolic action sequences (structured plans), instantiated by a library of parameterized primitive skills on the robot
setting.simulator: AI2-THOR (data collection only); benchmark is static VQA
setting.privileged: none at test time (the graph is predicted from images; the real robot skills are task-specific, derived from teleoperation)

numbers.extra: Graph-then-Plan; accuracy % on multiple-choice VQA, unseen environments
numbers.evidence: Table 2 (Performance comparison on the MomaGraph-Bench), MomaGraph-R1 w/ Graph

numbers.eval_set_note: visual correspondence and multi-view reasoning tasks from BLINK
numbers.extra: scene graph generated first, then answer
numbers.evidence: Table 3 (BLINK and MomaGraph-Bench): MomaGraph-R1 BLINK 63.5, MomaGraph-Bench 77.5

numbers.eval_set_note: 10 trials with different camera viewpoints, RobotEra Q5, one multi-step task
numbers.evidence: "80% success rate in graph generation, 87.5% success rate in planning ... overall task success rate of 70% over 10 trials"

numbers_note: The abstract's "+11.4%" is the gain over the best open-source baseline in the abstract but the text calls it relative over Qwen2.5-VL-7B w/ Graph (60.2→71.6, i.e. +11.4 points). Table 3 is BLINK plus the correspondence subset of the benchmark, and its exact evaluation protocol is not fully specified.
results: MomaGraph-R1 reaches 71.6% overall on MomaGraph-Bench with a graph, +11.4 points over its base Qwen2.5-VL-7B (60.2) and above all open-source baselines (next is LLaVA-OV at 55.6). It matches GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5-Pro (71.6) and is slightly below Claude-4.5-Sonnet (73.9). It also leads open-source models on BLINK correspondence (63.5) and reaches 70% overall success in a real-robot long-horizon task.
limitations: The benchmark is multiple-choice VQA generated with VLMs and manually verified, with a small training set (~1,050 graphs). The real-robot evaluation is a single task with 10 trials, so the evidence for planning gains is mostly offline.
Low-level control relies on task-specific primitive skills from teleoperation. The state-aware dynamic update is described conceptually but not quantitatively evaluated.
Errors compound across stages (graph generation 80%, planning 87.5% given a correct graph), with spatial relation errors and missing nodes.
